name: ModProfiler
teaser: Find the mod eating your frames: live CPU time per installed mod, without disabling any
description:
When the game stutters, the usual answer is to disable half your mods and bisect. This one answers directly: it stopwatches every mod’s own code - Harmony patches, frame methods, coroutines - and shows live what each costs per frame. Like Dubs Performance Analyzer in RimWorld, the numbers rank your mods usefully; they are not a frame-exact truth. See at a glance whether the garbage collector is on and how fast your raid is really allocating - and how much of a slow frame is your mod versus the game itself.

Features

  • One row per mod: average and peak ms, calls per frame, share of the frame, total. Sort by any column, expand a mod for its priciest methods.
  • A GC & heap panel in both UIs’ headers: the collector’s live on/off state (EFT turns it off for the whole raid above ~25 GB RAM - the heap then only ever grows, which is expected, not a leak), the managed heap size and its peak, and the allocation rate.
  • A curated EFT (vanilla) row measures seven of the game’s own per-frame methods
    • world tick, bot AI, player update, ballistics, the interaction prompt - next to your mods, honestly labeled as inclusive of any mod patch on the same method.
  • Pause, rescan and CSV export with per-frame values, deltas since the last export, and a sidecar carrying spikes, patch failures and machine context.
  • With the optional Anvil-WebOverlay library it opens as its own window and adds µs per call (which exposes rows that are mostly measurement overhead), a spike log for stuttering frames, amber GC ticks on the frame graph, trend graphs, a filter and tooltips.
  • A ▲ growth marker flags a mod or method whose live instance count keeps climbing for minutes without falling back, and CSV exports can write themselves on a timer.

Installation and first use

Extract the ZIP into your SPT folder and press F11 in game. The first activation instruments all mod code and freezes the game for a few seconds - normal, once per session. In a raid press Rescan once: some mods only patch at raid start.

Requirements

  • SPT 4.1.x, built and tested there. Client-side only, no server component.
  • Required: Anvil-WebOverlay 1.8.8+ for the window (needs the WebView2 runtime and windowed/borderless mode). Without it a built-in overlay shows the core table.

Limits

  • Measuring carries a small fixed cost, measured on your machine at every scan, that partly lands inside every measured value, so no row can read below that floor - for a very frequently called mod that floor can be most of its row (µs/Call shows where).
  • Times are inclusive, so the percentages can add up past 100.
  • Indirect load is only partly visible: a mod that spawns more bots costs time inside the engine, not in its own code - the EFT (vanilla) row gives a partial answer for bot AI and world tick, the GC & heap panel one for the collector. Rendering, culling and physics outside those seven curated methods stay invisible.

Support

Open a GitHub issue with your ModProfiler and SPT versions, short repro steps and your complete BepInEx/LogOutput.log - plus a CSV export if it is about the numbers.
